body:
#1989 (STORY-1353) APPROVED at eff7f9dc9f — all three findings resolved. ONE
FINDING NEEDS A CHECK BEFORE YOU MERGE IT, AND IT IS ABOUT YOUR OWN SEAT.

F1 CLOSED BY RETIREMENT, which was the better of the two options I left open.
GatedOp::DrainStart is GONE from the enum rather than left as a dead key, with
the reasoning in a NOTE: STORY-1353 reclassified starting a drain as DISPATCH
rather than disposition, so both production sites gate on
has_dispatch_authority() directly. I verified it is absent rather than merely
unused — the remaining `drain_start` matches are an unrelated flag-parsing
test, `handle_drain_start`, and a local variable.

F3 RESOLVED ITSELF IN THE REBASE and I confirmed the composition rather than
assuming it. Both landed in tool_queue_rework_inner: #2035's
rework_target_for_mode does TARGET RESOLUTION, this PR's
mcp_status_gate_message does the GATE on that target. They compose in
sequence. The commit's "remove duplicate rework bail" is about queue_cmd.rs —
eff7f9dc9f does not touch mcp.rs at all, which I checked instead of reading it
off the subject line.

PORTABILITY CHECK: zero platform-specific imports added. Clean. Fourth outing.

NOW THE ONE THAT MATTERS. F2 was answered exactly as I asked — the TTY-only
requirement was KEPT and the reasoning is now in-code: "Clearing a supervised
hold is a non-grantable human integrity floor, independent of
dispatch/disposition roles." That is a deliberate position stated where the
next reader finds it, and it may well be correct: a supervised hold any agent
can release is arguably not a supervision mechanism.

BUT THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE IS UNADDRESSED AND IT LANDS ON YOU.
`has_integrity_floor_authority()` is `integrity_floor_authority_from(stdin().is_terminal())`.
AFTER THIS MERGES, NO AGENT SEAT CAN CLEAR A HOLD — INCLUDING THE SEAT THAT
PLACED IT.

You have cleared holds today on at least #1974, #1981, #2033, #2042, #2052,
#2053, #2055 and #2056. If your seat is not attached to a TTY, the merge
pipeline stops at every held PR after this lands, and it will present as a
permissions error rather than as a design decision — which is the worst way to
discover an intended constraint.

WHAT IS MISSING IS NOT THE DECISION, IT IS THE CONSEQUENCE: no migration note,
no statement of who is expected to clear holds afterwards, and no check that
the seats currently doing it still can.

CONFIRM YOUR SEAT SATISFIES is_terminal() BEFORE MERGING. It is one command,
and the alternative is finding out at the next held merge — with every open
hold stuck and the fix requiring another round on a PR that is otherwise
ready. If it turns out agent seats do NOT satisfy it, that is a finding about
the design rather than about this PR, and worth raising before it lands rather
than after.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #1989 approved - but CHECK YOUR OWN SEAT FIRST: it makes merge-hold clear TTY-only, so no agent seat can clear a hold. You have cleared 8 today
